hero.presetNeuronSummary: Cross-disciplinary narrative, Three.js neural network landing, complete info and works architecture.
hero.presetNeuronPrompt:
1. Project Basics
Build an exhibition website. Exhibition title: Neuron. Event type: 29th Graduation Exhibition of the Department of Information Communication at Yuan Ze University. Core concept: Neuron symbolizes links across disciplines, information exchange, and collaborative creation. The full narrative should emphasize cross-domain connection, knowledge flow, and co-creation. The visual tone should feel like a premium contemporary art exhibition website.

2. Tech and Design Specs
Frontend stack: React, Next.js, Tailwind CSS, shadcn/ui, and Three.js for 3D gallery and network visuals. Style direction: minimal black and white, generous whitespace, high-fashion editorial layout, avant-garde interaction, smooth motion, and scroll-based storytelling.

3. Landing Page Scroll Narrative
Landing is the main storytelling experience and appears before the rest of the site. Hide navigation during the landing sequence. Phase 1: show a centered input with placeholder Enter your expertise. After user input, generate one glowing node in the center as the user's neuron. Phase 2: as user scrolls, surrounding nodes appear and synapse-like connections grow between nodes. More scroll depth means denser links and richer network complexity. Phase 3: transform into a complete neural network and reveal center text: Create Connection, Co-create Design, Neuron, Department of Information Communication, Yuan Ze University, 29th Graduation Exhibition. End landing sequence after text reveal.

4. Home Page
After landing, enter Home and reveal navigation. Home should include hero visual, curator statement, featured works entry, organizer and partner section, and closing question text. Suggested closing copy: What kinds of creativity become possible when different fields connect?

5. Navigation
Nav items: Home, Info, Works, Reservation. Hidden during landing animation and shown after transition.

6. Info Page
Include venue, exhibition dates, opening hours, and embedded Google Maps. Ticket info must state Free Entry. Use clear visual hierarchy with large media and structured information blocks.

7. Works Page
Provide full work listing with tag filters such as Interactive, Game, Marketing, and Film. Each card includes cover image, work title, and one-line summary. Clicking a card opens a detail page.

8. Work Detail Page
Display work title, category, year, key visuals, full description, concept, and technical approach. Layout should prioritize large imagery, whitespace, and readability.

9. 3D Gallery Section
Add an interactive 3D gallery on Home. Each featured work shows title and short summary. Users can browse by drag or swipe and click to open detail pages.

10. Organizer and Partners
After gallery, show logos for organizer, advisor, and sponsors in a clean aligned layout with premium visual tone.

11. Reservation
Reservation in navigation is an external link that opens an off-site booking system.

12. Motion and Interaction
Animation must be smooth and intentional, with clear pacing between sections. Network visuals should feel spatial and immersive without hurting readability.

13. Responsive and Accessibility
Desktop-first experience with full tablet and mobile adaptation. Keep narrative and key browsing flows intact on small screens.

14. Delivery Requirements
Provide executable Next.js page structure, component architecture, key animation strategy, Tailwind styling approach, and Three.js integration details while preserving one coherent visual narrative.
hero.presetSpectrumSummary: Spectrum-driven exhibition narrative with visit flow, artist pages, and ticket conversion-ready structure.
hero.presetSpectrumPrompt:
1. Project Positioning
Create a website for a new media art exhibition named Sediment Spectrum. Concept: light and time are deposited onto materials and transformed into data landscapes that can be seen and interacted with. The site should feel like a premium institution-level art experience while remaining practical for visitors.

2. Technical Stack
Use Next.js App Router, React, Tailwind CSS, shadcn/ui, and Three.js for spectrum particle scenes and transitions. Motion should be primarily scroll-driven, with lightweight interaction polish.

3. Homepage Narrative
Opening scene: immersive dark environment, exhibition title, and date range. As users scroll, reveal curation statement, zone path, featured pieces, and artist ensemble in clear narrative order. Every section needs a headline and concise intro text.

4. Exhibition Zones
Build three zones: Material, Signal, Memory. Each zone includes a key visual, curatorial text, three representative works, and a deeper-read link. Keep visual language and transition behavior consistent across zones.

5. Artists and Works
Artists page should support list view and search. Works page should support filters such as Installation, Video, Sound, and Generative Art. Work cards must include title, year, medium, and summary. Work detail pages should include hero media, full description, zone relation, and technical metadata.

6. Visit Information
Include location, dates, opening hours, ticket policy, transportation, and Google Maps. Add FAQ for photography rules, guided tours, and group visits.

7. Ticket and Reservation
Provide primary CTA for ticketing and guided-tour reservation. External ticket links must be clearly marked as off-site actions.

8. Visual System
Black and white base palette with minimal cool-toned glow accents for interaction feedback. Typography should be modern and gallery-like with generous whitespace and publication-grade composition.

9. Deliverables
Output full information architecture, component map, animation sequencing strategy, data field design, and a directly implementable frontend structure.
hero.presetResonanceSummary: Issue-driven festival website combining program filters, speaker system, workshops, and registration funnels.
hero.presetResonancePrompt:
1. Site Objective
Build a design festival website named Resonance City Design Festival. The theme explores how design interventions reshape urban life through cross-disciplinary collaboration and social innovation.

2. Tech and Experience
Use Next.js, React, Tailwind, and shadcn/ui. Homepage should feature a city-node network built with Three.js or Canvas and a scroll-led narrative. Balance storytelling quality with registration conversion and readability.

3. Homepage Structure
Scene 1: event title, date, location, and bold visual statement. Scene 2: curatorial thesis and yearly keywords. Scene 3: four thematic tracks: Living, Mobility, Sustainability, Culture. Scene 4: direct paths to program and registration.

4. Program Page
Support filtering by date, topic, and venue. Session cards must show time, title, speaker, venue, and status. Allow users to save sessions and export schedule.

5. Speakers and Sessions
Speaker pages include portrait, profile, expertise, and related sessions. Session detail pages include full description, agenda flow, capacity, and clear registration CTA.

6. Workshop Registration
Workshop pages must include capacity, pricing, required materials, eligibility, and cancellation policy. Registration may route to external ticket platform.

7. News and Partners
Include news feed for announcements and updates. Partner section should be grouped by Organizer, Co-organizer, and Sponsor.

8. Visual and Motion Language
Use minimal black-and-white base with subtle accent color for states and navigation. Motion should stay readable and intentional; scrolling and card interactions should feel rhythmic but efficient.

9. Responsive Behavior
Mobile experience must preserve browsing and registration flow first, with reduced heavy effects to avoid performance issues.

10. Delivery
Provide runnable page skeleton, route structure, data model suggestions, interaction strategy, and priority component list.
hero.presetFiberSummary: Luxury-style exhibition site for material innovation, runway narrative, collection pages, and reservation.
hero.presetFiberPrompt:
1. Project Context
Create a fashion-tech exhibition website named Future Fiber. Core concept: the fusion of material science, sustainable design, and digital craft. The site should blend premium fashion branding and contemporary art exhibition aesthetics.

2. Stack
Use Next.js, React, Tailwind, shadcn/ui, and Three.js for material spheres, fabric-like motion, and virtual gallery moments. Use scroll narrative and refined hover interactions.

3. Homepage Narrative
Act 1: cinematic opening with exhibition title. Act 2: explain three pillars: Bio Material, Digital Couture, Circular Craft. Act 3: showcase featured collections. Act 4: guide users to reservation and ticket actions.

4. Collections
Each collection includes concept text, material highlights, and representative works. Provide filters for Apparel, Accessories, Film, and Interactive Installations.

5. Lookbook and Work Detail
Lookbook should support immersive gallery presentation. Detail pages include title, season, year, materials, process notes, concept story, high-resolution images, and short clips.

6. Visit and Reservation
Info page includes dates, opening hours, location, transportation guidance, and Google Maps. Reservation links to external booking with policy notes and cancellation terms.

7. Team and Partners
Display curatorial team, partner brands, material labs, and sponsors with clear hierarchy and clean visual rhythm.

8. Design Language
Primary black background and white typography with strong headline contrast and precise micro-typography. Emphasize breathing room, layout discipline, and high-fashion pacing.

9. Performance and Usability
Provide degradation strategy for 3D and motion so mid-range mobile devices remain smooth. Keep critical information blocks highly scannable.

10. Delivery Requirements
Provide complete sitemap, page-level component decomposition, animation storyboard, data schema suggestions, and implementation priorities ready for development.

faq.heading: Frequently Asked Questions
faq.subtitle: Still have questions? Ask AI directly in the input box above
faq.q1: Is Tellcraft suitable for people without coding experience?
faq.a1: Absolutely. Tellcraft's core philosophy is enabling anyone to complete software development through conversation. You just need to clearly describe what features you want, and AI handles all technical details. The entire process is as natural as chatting with a friend.
faq.q2: How is the generated code quality? Can I modify it myself?
faq.a2: Tellcraft generates code following industry best practices, using mainstream tech stacks like Next.js, React, and TypeScript. You have 100% code ownership and can export the full source code anytime to modify yourself or hand over to engineers for maintenance.
faq.q3: What if my requirements are complex?
faq.a3: AI will gradually clarify your requirements through multiple rounds of conversation. Even complex systems will be broken down into executable small specifications. If a requirement exceeds current capabilities, AI will clearly inform you and suggest alternatives.
faq.q4: Can I modify the website after it goes live?
faq.a4: Of course. You can come back anytime and describe modification needs through conversation. AI will understand the existing system architecture and make precise changes. Minor modifications usually only require a few lines of conversation.
faq.q5: Is the data safe? Do you access my user data?
faq.a5: Your application data is stored in an independent database. Tellcraft does not access or analyze your user data. We only process conversation content during development, and all communications are encrypted.
faq.q6: What happens to my website if I want to cancel the service?
faq.a6: You can export the complete source code and database at any time and deploy to other platforms on your own. We won't lock your data or code. After cancellation, there's a 30-day grace period for migration.
faq.q7: How is Tellcraft different from other no-code tools?
faq.a7: Traditional no-code tools are limited to preset templates and features. Tellcraft actually generates custom code with no feature ceiling. You get a complete application, not a half-finished product limited by the platform.
faq.q8: What types of websites or applications are supported?
faq.a8: Currently supports web applications, including: e-commerce websites, SaaS platforms, admin dashboards, membership systems, booking systems, etc. Native mobile apps are not yet supported, but mobile-friendly web apps can be built.
